newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander buys back its shares from Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Santander buys back its shares from Nomura.

text.p: Spanish bank Santander said on Friday it had bought back a 1.3 percent stake of its own shares from Japanese broker Nomura Securities for approximately 25 billion pesetas.
A Santander spokesman said Nomura had originally taken the stake as part of a cooperative accord on investment banking agreed in 1989 that was now out-of-date.

Under the deal, Nomura took a 1.5 percent stake which was reduced to 1.3 percent by 1997, and had the option to buy 10 percent of Santander unit Banco Santander de Negocios (BSN). However, Nomura did not take up the option and it expired last August.
The sale of the 1.3 percent stake took place as a block trade during market hours last Wedneday, Santander said.
